html:
SMTO-SKL-0163 — Your saved GitHub account isn't allowed to use this repository

GUID: 6b13b3da-8bb1-5c25-8483-f2569f58b5d3
Slug: github-repository-not-authorized
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • This repository isn't on the list of repositories your saved GitHub account may use in SMTO. SMTO stopped before doing anything in it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the repository name in your request is correct, written as owner/name. A small typo makes SMTO treat it as a different repository that isn't on your list.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select your GitHub account entry, open Value, select Reveal & edit value, add the repository as owner/name to the authorized repositories list, and select Save. SMTO only works with repositories you've listed for that account.
  3. On github.com, make sure your token's repository access also includes this repository. Both SMTO's list and GitHub's token settings must allow the repository.
  4. If another saved account already has this repository, repeat your request and pick that account by typing @ and choosing it. That account is already allowed to use the repository.

What success looks like

  • Repeating your request completes and shows the repository you asked about.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Only add repositories you actually want SMTO to use.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested owner/repo is not in the selected GitHub Account profile's authorized_repositories allowlist and no task resource grant covers it.

What this means

  • The requested owner/repo is absent from the account profile's authorized_repositories allowlist. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • The requested owner/repo is absent from the account profile's authorized_repositories allowlist.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the explicit profile allowlist and independent token repository selection.

How to fix it

  • GitHubService.execute and authorization.check deny any owner/repo absent from value.authorized_repositories (case-insensitive) unless a task access session explicitly permits it. Add the exact owner/repo to the profile's allowlist and to the PAT's repository selection on GitHub, or select an existing account that already authorizes it; access is never expanded automatically.
  • Explicitly authorize this exact repository in both the GitHub token selection and the account profile allowlist, or select the intended existing account. Access is never expanded automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended repository is deliberately authorized in both applicable controls.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
